author: human
request:
Feature request: filter the vet list by specialty. Three product decisions
come with it, made here as the product owner:

- Non-goal NG-9 is narrowed: free-text veterinarian search stays out of
  scope, but filtering the directory by an attribute it already shows is in.
  Record the narrowing the way the project records non-goal changes.
- The JSON endpoint at /vets is reinstated as a supported surface — this
  filter is its first requested capability. Mint a fresh requirement for it;
  the withdrawn REQ-VET-002 stays withdrawn and its id is not reused.
- The filter is a URL contract only. Neither surface gains a form, dropdown,
  or other page control in this request; pagination links carry the
  parameter so filtered pages stay navigable. A visible control may come as
  a follow-up request.

Both vet list surfaces accept an optional `specialty` query parameter:

- /vets.html?specialty=<name> — the HTML page shows only vets holding that
  specialty; pagination applies to the filtered list.
- /vets?specialty=<name> — the JSON endpoint returns only those vets.

Matching is on the whole specialty name, case-insensitive — not a prefix. A
specialty matching no vet yields the normal page or JSON document with an
empty vet list (HTTP 200). An empty or whitespace-only value behaves as if
the parameter were absent, like the empty owner search. Without the parameter
both endpoints behave as today. Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Staff and programs can narrow the veterinarian directory to one specialty
summary: Both veterinarian directory surfaces, the HTML page and the reinstated JSON list, accept an optional specialty in the address and list only veterinarians holding it. The match is on the whole name in any letter case. The URL is the whole contract: no page control is added.
acceptance_criteria: [REQ-VET-003] GET /vets with no specialty parameter returns every veterinarian with their specialties, as today; this JSON list is now a supported surface.
[REQ-VET-003] GET /vets.html?specialty=<name> lists only veterinarians holding that specialty, and pagination (page count and pages) applies to the narrowed list.
[REQ-VET-003] On a narrowed /vets.html page, every pagination link carries the same specialty parameter, so following it stays narrowed.
[REQ-VET-003] GET /vets?specialty=<name> returns only veterinarians holding that specialty.

[REQ-VET-003] Matching is on the whole specialty name, case-insensitive: 'radiology', 'Radiology', and 'RADIOLOGY' match the same veterinarians on both surfaces; a prefix such as 'radio' matches no veterinarian.
[REQ-VET-003] A specialty no veterinarian holds, including a name the clinic does not have, returns HTTP 200 with the normal page or JSON document and an empty veterinarian list on both surfaces.
[REQ-VET-003] An empty or whitespace-only specialty value behaves exactly as if the parameter were absent, on both surfaces.
[REQ-VET-001] Without the specialty parameter, /vets.html behaves as today: every veterinarian, paged, with 'none' for a veterinarian holding no specialty.
non_goals: Free-text veterinarian search (NG-9, narrowed but still declining it).
Any form, dropdown, link set, or other page control for choosing a specialty on either surface; a visible control may come as a separate follow-up request.
Naming more than one specialty in one request.
Filtering by any attribute other than specialty.
Showing on the page which specialty narrows it.
Supporting any machine-readable format other than JSON.
Any change to either surface's behavior without the specialty parameter.
Reusing or reviving REQ-VET-002, which stays withdrawn.
notes: Owner decisions quoted from intake line 1. REQ-VET-003 is the one fresh requirement the owner asked to mint: it reinstates the JSON list and carries the filter on both surfaces, because the owner called the filter the endpoint's first capability. PRD edits: NG-9 row and preamble narrowed; directory section gains REQ-VET-003, its Done-when bullets, and edge cases 2-4; the old edge case 2 (known defect: unrequested JSON route) is retired because the route is now required; the REQ-VET-002 Superseded entry keeps the ID withdrawn and points to REQ-VET-003; Context mentions the published list. Non-goal ADR written: docs/adr/2026-09-29-non-goal-free-text-veterinarian-search.md. The docs/adr/README.md index row for it is outside my write scope and needs adding by its owner. Open questions (narrowest reading, owner gave no further answers, recorded in PRD Open Questions): a padded non-empty value such as ' surgery ' has no contract and is left to design; multiple specialties, showing the active specialty, a visible control, JSON paging, and non-JSON formats are all unrequested. Test names are one per behavior; the case-insensitive/prefix test and the blank test are data-driven across both surfaces. Edge-case coverage: PRD directory edge cases 2 (a vet with several specialties is listed when any one is named) and 3 (a vet with no specialty never appears in a narrowed directory) belong in the fixture of theVetPageShouldListOnlyVetsHoldingTheRequestedSpecialty; edge case 4 is theSpecialtyFilterShouldYieldAnEmptyListWhenNoVetHoldsTheSpecialty.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The slice extends the vet feature package along the owner feature's existing paged-search seam: an optional request parameter in the controller feeds a Spring Data derived query that the repository pages (OwnerController/OwnerRepository; system-design.md § Contracts). No new module, layer, or type. The adjustments: VetRepository gains a paged and an unpaged derived query matching the whole specialty name ignoring case (Distinct, so each veterinarian appears once), both uncached per the new ADR 2026-09-29-uncached-narrowed-directory-reads. VetController binds an optional String specialty on both routes, strips surrounding whitespace, and treats an empty result as absent, which is binding normalization per architecture-principles.md § pattern catalog, Web controller row. The page adds the normalized value to the model so vetList.html can carry it in page links. The JSON route returns the Vets wrapper filled from either read. Whitespace design call: ' surgery ' matches surgery. Surrounding whitespace is stripped with the same whitespace test that makes a blank value absent, so one normalization covers both cases; inner whitespace and letter case pass through unchanged, and the query ignores case. Recorded in system-design.md § Contracts, paragraph 'Narrowing the veterinarian directory'. Basis for the covering claim: grep/read of VetController, VetRepository, Vets, vetList.html, CacheConfiguration, and the h2 schema and seed data (no IDE oracle connected, so this is the weaker basis).
integration_points: Binding, both routes (/vets.html and /vets): the new input is a request-scoped @RequestParam(required = false) String specialty. No persisted type is bound, so no allow-list is needed; the existing page int param is unchanged. Normalization: strip, and empty counts as absent (architecture-principles.md, Web controller row; security-principles.md § Trust Boundaries, external input row).

Double, repository boundary (query semantics): the real Spring Data VetRepository over embedded H2 seed data in the existing @DataJpaTest seat ClinicServiceTests. Whole-name match, case variants, the 'radio' prefix, an unknown name, a veterinarian with several specialties (Linda Douglas), and one with none (James Carter) are proven here, because only the real query can prove them.
Double, framework transport: MockMvc (the sanctioned transport double) in VetControllerTests.

Double, repository seen from the controller: the existing @MockitoBean VetRepository stub in VetControllerTests (framework stub). Seed data holds at most two veterinarians per specialty, below one page, and VetRepository has no write path, so no real fixture reaches a second narrowed page. A hand-written fake would re-implement the query it stands in for. Stubs cover only the new narrowed methods and the existing unnarrowed ones; tests assert the normalized value is forwarded and that blank input calls the unnarrowed read.

Template: vetList.html page links (numbered, first, previous, next, last) carry specialty only when present, using Thymeleaf link-parameter syntax @{/vets.html(page=${i},specialty=${specialty})}. The existing '__${...}__' preprocessed form stays confined to the integer page number.

patterns.description: paged search: optional request param, repository Page, pagination model attributes
derived paged query method on a Spring Data Repository interface
narrowed reads carry no @Cacheable; unnarrowed reads keep theirs

risks.risk: Template expression injection: the caller-supplied specialty in a Thymeleaf '__${...}__' preprocessing expression or a concatenated href string is evaluated as an expression (security-principles.md § Realization, cross-site scripting row; request-derived value into markup).
risks.mitigation: Pass specialty only through link-parameter syntax, which URL-encodes it. Never preprocess or concatenate it into th:href. The security reviewer checks every link in vetList.html.

risks.risk: Cache growth from caller text: a @Cacheable narrowed method keys the unbounded vets cache by arbitrary strings (system-design.md § Scale and Load, Limits).
risks.mitigation: No cache annotation on the narrowed methods (ADR 2026-09-29-uncached-narrowed-directory-reads).

risks.risk: Veterinarian directory, narrowed row in § Scale and Load: the join through specialties could list a veterinarian twice when two specialties differ only by case, or when a join row is duplicated (the H2 vet_specialties has no uniqueness constraint).
risks.mitigation: Derived query with Distinct; the database pages it. Bounded path, simplest readable form.

risks.risk: Case-insensitive match portability across H2, MySQL, and PostgreSQL (system-design.md § Persistence records that case handling differs per vendor).
risks.mitigation: Use Spring Data IgnoreCase, which applies upper() to both sides in the query itself and does not depend on column collation. Never use native SQL or string-built JPQL (security-principles.md § Realization, injection row).

risks.risk: REQ-VET-001 regression: an unnarrowed page gaining a dangling 'specialty' link parameter, or a changed repository call.
risks.mitigation: Add the link parameter only when specialty is present, and keep unnarrowed requests on the existing cached findAll reads. The existing showVetListHtml and showResourcesVetList tests keep passing.

notes: Autofix audit: the log holds no design-doc-autofix records, so there was nothing to audit. Design-doc writes this dispatch: system-design.md Overview (the veterinarian directory is the one JSON surface); § Contracts, a new paragraph 'Narrowing the veterinarian directory' plus REQ-VET-003 on the Vet, Specialty, Vets, VetRepository, VetController, and CacheConfiguration rows; a new § Scale and Load (two directory rows plus the Limits line for the unbounded, page-keyed vet cache); § Security Context inputs and outputs; § Known Defects, the retired row for the unrequested machine-readable route, which now serves REQ-VET-003; Open Questions item 5 wording. New ADR docs/adr/2026-09-29-uncached-narrowed-directory-reads.md. docs/adr/README.md index rows added for it and for the product expert's non-goal ADR 2026-09-29-non-goal-free-text-veterinarian-search.md. Doctor check: 0 failures. For product-requirements-expert: docs/prd.md Open Questions still lists 'whether a named specialty with spaces around it matches' as open. Design has settled it (surrounding whitespace is stripped, so ' surgery ' matches surgery); that bullet can be retired or pointed at the design paragraph. The implementer may add a test asserting a padded value matches, since design fixes the behavior.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Injection into data access: the request-supplied specialty reaches only the Spring Data derived methods VetRepository.findDistinctBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase(String) / (String, Pageable), which bind it as a query parameter. A sweep of added lines for '@Query|createQuery|nativeQuery' over `python3 scripts/changeset.py` returned no hits. IgnoreCase derives an equality comparison, not LIKE, so '%' and '_' in the input are not wildcards.

XSS and template-expression evaluation: the narrowing specialty reaches vetList.html only through Thymeleaf link-expression parameters (e.g. `@{/vets.html(page=${i},specialty=${specialty})}`), which URL-encode the value and attribute-escape the href. The path is fixed, so no javascript: or data: URI can be formed. The change also removes the `__${...}__` preprocessing from vetList.html pagination links, and a grep -F '__${' of src/main/resources/templates no longer matches vetList.html. No th:utext was added (sweep of added lines).
Mass assignment: both routes bind the specialty as a plain `@RequestParam Optional<String>`. No persisted type is bound, which matches system-design.md:82.

Resource exhaustion: narrowed reads are deliberately uncached (the VetRepository javadoc and ADR 2026-09-29-uncached-narrowed-directory-reads), so caller text cannot grow the unbounded 'vets' cache. The paged route is paged by the database, and the unpaged JSON route is bounded by the vet count, as the existing unnarrowed route is.
Normalization at the boundary: VetController.normalize strips whitespace and treats an empty value as absent, so blank input falls back to the existing unnarrowed read.

Secrets and logging: a sweep of added lines for 'password|secret|token|apikey|credential|log.' found only the system-design.md Security Context prose describing datasource credentials from the environment. No credential or log statement was added.

Supply chain: build.gradle, settings.gradle, and gradle/ are unchanged (`git status --short`). The resolved runtimeClasspath shows Spring Boot 4.1.1, Thymeleaf 3.1.5.RELEASE, and jackson-databind 3.1.5 (tools.jackson). dependencyCheckAnalyze is not configured, so no NVD match ran in this review.

recommendations: Equivalence-class overlap: in VetControllerTests blankSpecialtiesOnBothSurfaces, SPACES and TAB pass through the same strip-then-empty path. Surrounding-whitespace stripping (theSpecialtyFilterShouldIgnoreSurroundingWhitespace) is asserted on the JSON surface only. The page surface runs the same normalize() but has no padded-value test, so a change that bypassed normalize() in showVetList would go uncaught for a non-blank padded value. This is not a Done-when bullet, which only requires blank values to match the unnarrowed request, so it is not a defect.

The ADR/design decision that narrowed reads bypass the vet cache (docs/system-design.md line 82, VetRepository javadoc) has no test. Nothing fails if someone adds @Cacheable to the narrowed queries, which would grow the cache without bound. The check needs a cache-enabled test slice; consider it if the project wants the ADR enforced. It is not one of the 8 Done-when bullets, so I did not raise it as a finding.

Not verified in this review: whether the pagination template block is guarded for totalPages 0. The empty-page test asserts status 200 and an empty listVets only, so it does not check the rendered pager for a zero-page result.

The whole-name, ignore-case and distinct query rule is tested against the real database via @DataJpaTest in ClinicServiceTests, so it is not covered only through a mocked repository.
